name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,773

entries.clue: Bike race that's foolhardy will go ahead (7)

blocks.note: a mad scheme is a foolhardy one
an event that will go ahead is on

annotation.surface: A reckless cycle race that the organisers insist will still take place.
annotation.walkthrough: A madison is a track-cycling relay race for teams of two, named after Madison Square Garden.
annotation.definitionFit: The madison is a named event in track cycling, so it is a bike race.

entries.clue: Film method for making pie crust? (6,8)

blocks.note: the cinema, and the straight definition
the surface reading is a kitchen question; the setter means a way of producing the letters P-I-E-C-R-U-S-T by moving the letters of another word

annotation.surface: A cook asks how to make the pastry for a pie.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a reverse anagram: the answer's second word, shaken up, spells PIE CRUST, and the first word is the instruction to shake it.
annotation.definitionFit: Moving pictures is an old name for film, the cinema.

entries.clue: Doctor with private swamp (5)

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
your own room is your private room

annotation.surface: A doctor who owns a private patch of marshland.
annotation.walkthrough: Swamp looks like a noun in the surface, but it is the verb: to swamp or drown something.
annotation.definitionFit: To swamp something is to flood it completely, to drown it.

entries.clue: Waves to friend at certain times (10)

blocks.note: heavy seas are big waves
as in pushing a door to, or on
an ally is a friend

annotation.surface: Someone who waves to a friend only now and then.
annotation.walkthrough: Waves reads as the verb of greeting, but it is the noun: the sea's waves.
annotation.definitionFit: Something that happens seasonally happens at certain times of year.

entries.clue: Boy you might love is one wanting love, thank goodness (6)

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so ONE goes without its O

blocks.note: surface padding that colours the definition: a boy an aunt or uncle would love; it gives no letters
ONE without O, since love is zero in tennis
the exclamation of relief

annotation.surface: A boy you could fall for turns out to be single, to your relief.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is romantic, but the love meant is family love; the second love is tennis zero, the letter O.
annotation.definitionFit: A nephew is a male relative, and the clue's boy is a son of a sibling.

entries.clue: Drink behind old man's decline (4,2)

indicators.note: the drink comes behind, after, the old man's

blocks.note: pa = father, the old man
to sup is to drink

annotation.surface: Drinking is blamed for an old man's deterioration.
annotation.walkthrough: Decline reads as a noun, a falling off, but it is the verb: to decline an offer is to pass it up.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: turning down an offer is both declining it and letting it go by.

entries.clue: Irish article headed by "Priest Eats Fish" (8)

indicators.note: the priest's P goes at the head, in front of IRISH ARTICLE

blocks.note: P is an abbreviation for priest
abbreviation for Irish
the indefinite article
to have a meal is to eat it

annotation.surface: A newspaper headline about a clergyman's dinner.
annotation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make it look like a headline, which hides that Fish is the plural definition and Eats is just HAS.
annotation.definitionFit: Piranhas are South American freshwater fish; fish serves as a plural here.

entries.clue: Bargain tin, lowest possible price? (4)

blocks.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
1p, one penny, written as I P

annotation.surface: A cheap tin of something in the shop, priced as low as it can go.
annotation.walkthrough: A snip is British slang for a bargain; 1p is one penny, the smallest British coin.
annotation.definitionFit: British informal usage: a purchase priced far below its worth gets called a snip.

entries.clue: Poles wearing uniform knocked off, lacking tools (9)

indicators.note: the poles have the uniform on top of them, so U sits above NS

blocks.note: U is Uniform in the phonetic alphabet
N and S, north and south poles
to knock someone off is to kill them

annotation.surface: Polish soldiers in uniform, killed because they had no equipment.
annotation.walkthrough: Poles looks like people from Poland; it is the two ends of the earth. Tools is used loosely for skills, the tools of a trade.
annotation.definitionFit: Unskilled means lacking skills, the tools of the trade a worker would bring.

entries.clue: With harvest moon outside all notice architect (6,8)

indicators.note: harvest moon sits outside, around, ALL and notice

blocks.note: bread with butter is bread and butter
to reap is to harvest
taken as written
an advertisement, a notice
Io is a moon of Jupiter

annotation.surface: Under the harvest moon, everyone takes notice of an architect.
annotation.walkthrough: Harvest moon reads as one phrase, the full moon of autumn, but the setter pulls the two words apart so they can wrap round the next two.
annotation.definitionFit: Andrea Palladio was the Italian Renaissance architect whose villas gave us Palladian style.

entries.clue: One bowed when playing lead in Shakespeare (5)

blocks.note: a bowed string instrument, pitched between violin and cello
the heroine of Twelfth Night

annotation.surface: An actor takes a bow after playing the lead in a Shakespeare play.
annotation.walkthrough: Bowed suggests an actor bowing at the curtain call, but it is the bow drawn across strings.
annotation.definitionFit: A viola is a bowed string instrument, and Viola is the heroine of Twelfth Night.

entries.clue: Clergyman welcomes family chatter (9)

indicators.note: the parson takes the family in

blocks.note: a parson is a parish priest
your kin are your family

annotation.surface: A vicar invites a talkative family into his house.
annotation.walkthrough: Michael Parkinson hosted Parkinson, a long-running British TV chat show, so he is a chatter in the sense of a chat-show host.
annotation.definitionFit: Parkinson made his name chatting to guests on television, so he is a chatter.

entries.clue: Number of cops that carry guns? (4,3,3)

definitions.text: Number of cops that carry guns?

blocks.note: reads as a head count of officers; the setter means a telephone number that summons them
British police mostly go unarmed, so armed cops point the solver across the Atlantic

annotation.surface: How many police officers are armed?
annotation.walkthrough: The enumeration (4,3,3) spells the digits out as words, a hint that the number is one you dial rather than count.
annotation.definitionFit: 911 is the emergency number you dial to reach American police.

entries.clue: Lord said walk on water (4)

indicators.note: said means spoken, so we want the sound of the word

blocks.note: a lord is a peer of the realm

annotation.surface: A lord who claimed to walk on water, like a miracle worker.
annotation.walkthrough: Walk on water sounds like a miracle, but it is a noun phrase: a walkway built out over the sea.
annotation.definitionFit: A pier is a walkway on stilts over the sea, a walk on water.

entries.clue: River Test suitable for plant (10)

blocks.note: the Indus flows through Pakistan
a trial is a test

annotation.surface: The River Test, a famous English trout stream, is a good place for a plant to grow.
annotation.walkthrough: River Test reads as one name, the Hampshire trout river, but it splits into a river and a test. Plant means a factory, not greenery.
annotation.definitionFit: Industrial equipment is fit for a plant, a factory.

entries.clue: Ghost hunter caught lots, not finished after a year (3-3)

indicators.note: MANY loses its last letter
caught and lots come after a year

blocks.note: p.a., per annum, is a year
c is caught in cricket scoring
MANY without its end

annotation.surface: A ghost hunter took a year to capture lots of spirits and still isn't done.
annotation.walkthrough: Ghost hunter sounds like a paranormal investigator, but Pac-Man is the arcade game hero who chases ghosts round a maze.
annotation.definitionFit: Pac-Man eats the ghosts in the maze after a power pill, so he hunts ghosts.

entries.clue: Naval officer getting over runs in unplumbed toilet (9)

indicators.note: over and runs go inside the toilet

blocks.note: a commode is a chair with a chamber pot, a toilet with no plumbing
o = over in cricket scoring
r = runs in cricket scoring

annotation.surface: A naval officer recovering from a bout of diarrhoea on a toilet without plumbing.
annotation.walkthrough: The toilet splits as COMMOD and E, with OR slotted between.
annotation.definitionFit: A commodore is a naval officer ranking above captain.

entries.clue: Glossy oil an awful pink (8)

indicators.note: an awful version of OIL AN is a scrambled one

blocks.note: a glossy is a magazine, a mag
anagram fodder

annotation.surface: A shiny oil paint in a dreadful shade of pink.
annotation.walkthrough: Glossy reads as an adjective describing the paint, but it is the noun: a glossy magazine.
annotation.definitionFit: Magnolia is a pale creamy pink colour, named after the flower.

entries.clue: Minister split trousers continually (8)

indicators.note: used as a verb: split pockets, trousers, continually

blocks.note: to rend is to split
for ever, continually

annotation.surface: A government minister keeps splitting his trousers.
annotation.walkthrough: Trousers looks like a noun, but it is the verb: to trouser is to pocket, so REND pockets EVER.
annotation.definitionFit: Reverend is the title of a clergyman, and by extension the clergyman himself, a church minister.

entries.clue: Rider who's got the hump has brawl in coach (8)

indicators.note: the brawl goes inside the coach

blocks.note: a railway coach is a car
a melee is a confused fight

annotation.surface: A grumpy passenger starts a fight on a bus.
annotation.walkthrough: To have the hump is British slang for being in a bad mood; here the rider has a hump under him, on a camel.
annotation.definitionFit: A cameleer rides a camel, so the rider literally sits on the hump.

entries.clue: Plain Cockney tough guy from the East End (6)

indicators.note: Cockneys drop their Hs, so HARD becomes 'ARD
read starting from the east end, the right-hand end of an across entry

blocks.note: HARD NUT, a tough guy, with the H dropped

annotation.surface: A plain-spoken Cockney hard man from London's East End.
annotation.walkthrough: Plain looks like an adjective for the Cockney, but it is the noun, a flat treeless land. The East End is the Cockney heartland of London.
annotation.definitionFit: Tundra is the vast treeless plain of the Arctic.

entries.clue: Seal I see beneath spar (6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, I C goes below MAST

blocks.note: a mast is a spar on a ship
I, then C, the letter whose name is 'see'

annotation.surface: A sailor spots a seal lying under a ship's spar.
annotation.walkthrough: Seal reads as the animal, but it is a sealant.
annotation.definitionFit: Mastic is a putty-like substance used to seal joints.

entries.clue: Noodles for everyone put on (4)

blocks.note: U is the British film rating meaning suitable for all
to don clothes is to put them on

annotation.surface: Someone serves noodles for the whole table.
annotation.walkthrough: For everyone looks like generosity, but it is the British film certificate U, meaning suitable for all ages.
annotation.definitionFit: Udon are thick Japanese wheat noodles.

entries.clue: See vessel lays up back in Black Sea port (10)

indicators.note: the whole string is read backwards

blocks.note: lo, as in lo and behold, means see
a pot is a vessel
to lay up stores is to save them

annotation.surface: A ship is laid up in a Black Sea harbour.
annotation.walkthrough: Vessel and port make it look nautical, but the vessel is a cooking pot and lays up means stockpiles.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by location: the Crimean naval city stands on the Black Sea coast and is home to Russia's Black Sea Fleet.

entries.clue: Polyhedron on board problem sir put up (5)

indicators.note: the answer is carried inside the words
in a down clue, the letters are read bottom to top

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of problem, all of sir and the start of put, written backwards

annotation.surface: A maths problem about a polyhedron is set on the board for the teacher.
annotation.walkthrough: On board looks like a blackboard, but it means carried aboard the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A prism is a solid with flat faces, so a polyhedron.

entries.clue: American insults upset Russian legislature (4)

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the letters upside down

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
insults slung at someone, as in mudslinging

annotation.surface: An American's insults annoy the Russian parliament.
annotation.walkthrough: Upset reads as annoy, but it is the reversal instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: The Duma is the lower house of the Russian parliament.

entries.clue: New menu in motel affected income (9)

indicators.note: a new menu is a rearranged one
the motel it sits in is disturbed too

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A new menu at a motel has changed its takings.
annotation.walkthrough: Both words are scrambled together; the menu sitting in the motel is just the surface picture.
annotation.definitionFit: An emolument is a salary or fee, a form of income.

entries.clue: Current film captures face of Everest covered with climbers (5)

indicators.note: the film holds the E inside it
the face is the front, so the first letter

blocks.note: I is the symbol for electric current
short for video
first letter

annotation.surface: A new documentary shows the face of Everest crowded with mountaineers.
annotation.walkthrough: Climbers reads as mountaineers on Everest, but they are climbing plants such as ivy.
annotation.definitionFit: An ivied wall is covered with ivy, a climbing plant.

entries.clue: Slow, steep A-road (6)

blocks.note: to ret flax is to steep it in water
taken as written
standard abbreviation

annotation.surface: A warning sign on a hilly main road.
annotation.walkthrough: Steep reads as a gradient, but it is the verb to soak. In Britain an A-road is a main road.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb, from Latin tardus, slow; engineers still speak of retarding ignition timing.

entries.clue: Dishevelled detective has line on company boss (7)

indicators.note: the line goes on, after, company

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
standard abbreviation
the umbo is the raised boss in the centre of a shield

annotation.surface: A scruffy detective has a lead on the head of a firm.
annotation.walkthrough: Boss reads as the head of the company, but it is a knob, the umbo of a shield.
annotation.definitionFit: Columbo, played by Peter Falk, is the TV detective famous for his rumpled raincoat.
